text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for model=rwd-model-3.2 tag=release-2026-03-15 weights=weightset-20260315-v2 tokenizer=v1.9
metrics-bot: Canary nodes (us-east-1) 5xx_rate=3.7% p95_latency=2.0s (baseline p95=1.2s)
elaine: paging oncall @sam — canary is spiking, seeing TokenizationError in logs, looks like tokenizer/weights mismatch
sam: oncall here, looking. what artifacts were bundled for this release?
elaine: release manifest: weights: weightset-20260315-v2.tar.gz (sha256:abc123...), tokenizer: vocab_v1.9.zip (sha256:def456...). CI expected vocab_v2.0 but pipeline shows v1.9 published after weights were built
mike: confirm — deployment job used tag release-2026-03-15 from registry. packaging pipeline had a late tokenizer push; it appears we didn't pin tokenizer sha when building weight bundle. Logs showing error sample:
```
ERROR TokenizationError: unknown token id 50213 at tokenizer.py:87
context: input="\uF02A..."
```
elaine: probable root cause = artifact mismatch (weights expecting vocab v2.0, runtime got v1.9)
sam: pausing rollout and flipping kill-switch for canary flag. initiating kill-switch now
sam: /ops set-feature-flag model_release_canary OFF (issued)
ops-bot: feature flag `model_release_canary` set to OFF by sam at 2026-03-15T18:14:12Z
sam: evicting canary pods to force fallback to stable model: `for p in $(kubectl get pods -l canary=release-2026-03-15 -o name); do kubectl delete $p; done`
mike: started pod evict, controllers are recreating pods but some nodes still cache tokenizer v1.9 from local cache. kicking off node-level cache purge where possible
elaine: initiating rollback to stable tag=release-20260301-stable and pin model to that tag until postmortem
infra-bot: rollback job queued id=98765, target tag=release-20260301-stable
sam: handing off to next oncall @nisha — summary: canary had mismatched tokenizer+weights -> 5xx spike on canary (~3.7%) -> paused + kill switch + pod eviction -> rollback in progress. customer impact: partial errors, mostly EU, approx 1.8% of prod requests affected. affected customers: acme-ecom (beta), studio-beta testers
nisha: ack, joining. ETA for rollback completion?
mike: estimate ~6m to drain and replace nodes with stable artifact, watching 5xx and p95
metrics-bot: Canary 5xx_rate down to 0.4% after evict; production 5xx_rate now 0.6% (was 0.9% during spike)
customer-ops: support notified, public status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/CS-41234 - posting interim message to impacted customers. ticket #CS-41234 linked to this thread
sam: creating postmortem ticket and tagging infra/ml-release teams. immediate action items: 1) block release until artifacts are checksum-pinned, 2) add pre-deploy verify step comparing tokenizer sha -> weights expected sha, 3) add canary probe for TokenizationError class
elaine: I'll open the PR for checksum pinning and pre-deploy check. also adding a CI gate to fail builds if tokenizer timestamp > weights build time by > 30s (to catch late pushes)
nisha: taking over monitoring. will hold thread for 30m post-stable and then close if metrics are green. thanks team :thumbsup:
elaine: one more note — ops-bot output showed feature-flag flip succeeded, but I'll follow up to ensure no leftover listeners trigger stale canaries
ops-bot: feature flag `model_release_canary` state=OFF (active)
mike: manual check done: nodes in eu-west-1 replaced with stable tag, tokenization errors dropped in logs
metrics-bot: prod 5xx_rate stable at 0.2% p95=1.18s across regions
customer-ops: customers updated, CS-41234 will be updated with remediation and ETA for postmortem
nisha: closing handoff note — oncall takeover complete. I'll keep watch and escalate if regression returns.
elaine: thanks everyone. postmortem follow-up: root cause = packaging race, mitigation = artifact pinning + predeploy checksum + canary tokenization probe.
